label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
**Subject: Tuesday reading club: new numbers, and an apology**

Dear Niamh,

Thank you for your email of 30 October about pausing the Tuesday club after Christmas. I understand why you raised it. The numbers in September were poor, and with the hall insurance going up I can see it was a fair question to ask. But things have changed a good deal in the last few weeks, and I wanted you to have the full picture before the review meeting on the 18th.

There's also something I need to own up to, and I'd rather you heard it from me than from anyone else. I'll come to that below.

First, the good news. Attendance has gone like this:

- September: 5 children most weeks
- Mid-October: 9
- Tuesday 3 November: 14

Fourteen children in the meeting room upstairs on a Tuesday afternoon, Niamh. I honestly didn't think I'd see it.

Part of what's made the difference is a donation from Declan Moran at the Salthill Book Nook. He gave us 120 books, mostly for the 6 to 9 age group, and a good few of them as Gaeilge. The children went through the boxes like it was Christmas morning, and having new books on the table every week has made a real difference.

It's more than numbers, too. Two sisters from a Ukrainian family started with us in October. At the end of each session now, the older girl reads to her little sister in English. The rest of the room goes quiet to listen to her. And there's one boy who wouldn't open a book at all in September. Last week he asked me could he take two home. I taught for a long time, and moments like that still stop me in my tracks.

So I'd ask you to look at these numbers again before the 18th and reconsider the pause. It would be a terrible pity to stop now, just when it has taken off. I know the insurance cost hasn't gone away, and if there's anything I can do to help make the case, or to look at ways of covering it, I'm more than willing.

Now for the other thing. A couple of weeks ago I met Orla Keane from the Corrib Courier at the farmers' market. I got carried away telling her all about the club, and before I knew it I'd said "come along any Tuesday." She has since been in touch and would like to come on Tuesday 24 November with a photographer.

I know well that anything like this has to go through you first, and that the policy is clear: no photographs of children without your sign-off and the parental consent forms. I was wrong not to check with you before saying anything to her, plain and simple. I'm sorry for putting you in that position.

Here is what I'd suggest. I'll ring Orla and tell her the visit is on hold until you've had a chance to decide. If you'd rather not go ahead, that's the end of it, and I'll let her down gently. If you do think it's worth doing, I'm very happy to collect the consent forms from the parents myself and make sure everything is in order well before anyone arrives with a camera. Any family that doesn't want their child photographed would of course be kept well out of it.

I do think the coverage could be wonderful for us. It could be good for the club, for Corrib Reading Partners, and maybe even for finding a few more volunteers. But only if it's done properly and done your way, and I should have started there.

Let me know how you'd like me to handle it. In the meantime I'll be in touch with Orla this week to put things on hold. And if it would help to have me at the meeting on the 18th, or to send you anything in writing beforehand, just say the word.

Thanks, Niamh, for everything you do to keep all of this going.

Warm regards,

[Your name]
